reconcile.note: Clarke reads John and the Synoptics as one sequence: Jesus carried the cross himself until weakness required Simon's help.

discrepancy.note: Strauss notes that John has Jesus carry his own cross while the Synoptics substitute Simon, treating the usual harmonizing move as an unproven assumption.

quotes.text: …according to the latter Jesus himself carried his cross thither, while the former state that one Simon a Cyrenian bore it in his stead. The commentators indeed, as if a real agreement were assumed as a matter of course, reconcile these statements thus…
quotes.attr: D. F. Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), §132.

quotes.text: According to the Synoptics, when Jesus is led away to be crucified, the Roman guard…find a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and compel him to carry the cross…The fourth Gospel, however, does not appear to know anything of this incident or of Simon of Cyrene, but distinctly states that Jesus bore his own cross.
quotes.attr: Walter R. Cassels (d. 1907), Supernatural Religion, vol. III (Complete ed., 1879), Part VI, ch. II.

sides.snippet: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.
sides.verseText: As they came out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name, and they compelled him to go with them, that he might carry his cross.

sides.verseText: He went out, bearing his cross, to the place called \"The Place of a Skull,\" which is called in Hebrew, \"Golgotha,\"
